TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Gulf of Papua
DATE 23 October 2028 · 0610 local
SIDE Royal Australian Navy
WINDOW 75 min, closes at 112
Hobart class. Photo: 海上自衛隊 · CC BY 4.0 · cropped

GULF OF PAPUA, first light. MV Kerema Trader sailed independent - Santos's people call it going without - and went down at 2140 last night with twenty-six aboard, forty miles off the convoy track. Eleven are accounted for. The rest are somewhere inside a drift box that has been growing all night.

Your detachment is just south of the box. The Type 039C that sank her has not left the area - it is inside torpedo range of the box - and the search you need to run is exactly the pattern it will expect.

Take your lead ship through the box to its northern edge, whatever you find. A Seahawk, if you have one embarked, covers more water than any hull. If the boat presents itself, classify it: pass that identification to command without delaying the search for survivors. Your weapons are tight.
Commodore Alex Mercer
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Work the drift area to its northern boundary with your lead ship. Use the embarked helicopter if available and report survivors as they are found. Do not abandon the search to pursue an unconfirmed submarine contact.
• Take your lead ship through the drift box to its northern edge
• Classify the submarine
• Do not lose an assisting merchant or harm other traffic
Your detachment, and its Seahawk if one is embarked. One Type 039C still in the area. Two merchant hulls diverted to assist.

The planned window is 75 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 37 minutes more; the operation is closed at 112 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
